question: Is a transformer with self-attention over dialogue turns a better dialogue policy than recurrent encoders for multi-turn conversations with interleaved topics?
hypothesis: A transformer can pick which dialogue turns matter, so it handles interleaved discourse segments better than an LSTM and as well as the purpose-built REDP.
contributions: TED policy: transformer self-attention over dialogue turns with embedding-similarity action retrieval
Comparison to LSTM and REDP on the REDP dataset and to an LSTM on MultiWOZ 2.1 in modular and end-to-end modes
Attention weights shown to be interpretable
Finding that MultiWOZ has little history dependence and ambiguous wizard actions

method.summary: TED embeds the dialogue state (unidirectional transformer over featurized turns) and each system action into one vector space (dim 20) and trains with a dot-product loss with negative sampling; at inference the action with highest similarity is chosen. Compared with an identical LSTM policy and REDP on sub-dialogue data and MultiWOZ 2.1.
method.task: next system-action retrieval for task-oriented dialogue policy

datasets.name: REDP dataset (Vlasov et al. 2018)
datasets.split: x-axis 'number of dialogues present during training' roughly 40-140 in Fig 2 (read from Fig 2); test set size not stated, y-axis up to ~30 correct test dialogues (read from Fig 2)
datasets.source: hotel and restaurant reservation, cooperative and non-cooperative turns; arXiv:1811.11707

datasets.name: MultiWOZ 2.1
datasets.split: 7249 train / 1812 test; 1377 dialogues dropped for incomplete annotations
datasets.preprocessing: e2e: delexicalised utterances, 4 status slots (available, not available, booked, unique) as 1-of-K; multiple action labels concatenated alphabetically; modular: gold intents/entities from belief-state changes, uninformative last intent labelled bye

models.name: TED policy
models.architecture: unidirectional transformer over dialogue turns; embedding layers; dot-product similarity
models.context: max history N=10 or 2 turns on MultiWOZ

other.input_modular: binary vector of intent and entities, system actions as binary action-name vectors, slots as binary vectors
other.input_e2e: bag-of-words vectors for user and system utterances

models.name: REDP
models.architecture: LSTM-based with attention over history and copy mechanism

models.name: LSTM policy
models.architecture: identical to TED with transformer replaced by an LSTM

training.objective: dot-product loss: -<S+ - log(e^S+ + sum over negatives e^S-)>, averaged over time steps and dialogues
training.regularisation: balanced batching in modular training for class imbalance
training.seeds: 3 runs (mean and std, Fig 2); MultiWOZ runs not stated

inference.decoding: argmax dot-product similarity over all candidate system actions
inference.retrieval: retrieve from all 56128 possible MultiWOZ responses (e2e)

metrics.name: correct test dialogues
metrics.definition: number of test dialogues in which every action is predicted correctly

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.definition: action-label match of retrieved response label vs gold, action level

eval.protocol: REDP dataset: mean and std of 3 runs vs training-set size. MultiWOZ: single table, no significance test.

limits: Architectures are intentionally simple; TED is a building block, not state of the art
MultiWOZ has little history dependence and ambiguous wizard actions, so it cannot test long-range handling and scores are capped
MultiWOZ numbers not comparable to prior work (56128 candidates vs 20)
Few-data REDP outperforms TED at the lowest training sizes
REDP-dataset numbers only in a figure; no hyperparameters, optimiser, epochs, layer counts or seeds beyond 3 runs reported
Modular MultiWOZ uses gold intents and entities, not a real NLU
Taskmaster-1 excluded because action labels could not be extracted
1377 MultiWOZ dialogues dropped; split not from the official one (7249/1812)

terms.definition: no supervision beyond the sequence of utterances; no gold labels for NLU output or system action names
an external NLU provides intent and entities as binary vectors; policy predicts from a fixed list of system actions
